status: Fictional held-out cases. Labels written by the rules lane on 13 November 2026, before the rules were run on them, and awaiting the owner's review.
replay: Lines arrive two seconds apart with one speaker label, as in a live transcript. Where a case has an existingCue, that cue is on screen after its source line. userName, when present, is the session-only name from Settings.

events.text: Someone could book the hall for the bake sale.
We'll pick that up at the committee meeting next month. On to the raffle.

expected.reason: The speaker puts the booking off to a later meeting and starts another subject.

events.text: Someone should update the volunteer rota.
Let's leave room in it for the new volunteers.

existingCue.text: Who will update the volunteer rota?

expected.reason: Leaving room in the rota is about the rota, not putting it off; it still has no owner.

events.text: Someone should write the welcome letter this week.
Let's leave the poster design for another meeting.

existingCue.text: Who will write the welcome letter?

expected.reason: The poster was put off, not the letter; the letter still has no owner.

events.text: The plant sale is happening soon, so we need a date for the flyers.
Sorry, scratch that, the plant sale was cancelled.

existingCue.text: What date is the plant sale?

expected.reason: The speaker takes back the line the question came from.

events.text: Someone should collect the keys from the office.
Oh wait, I said Tuesday earlier for the delivery and I meant Thursday.

expected.reason: The correction is about the delivery day; nobody has taken the keys.

events.text: We could hold it in either the hall or the marquee.
Oh, hang on, the marquee went back to the hire company last week, so it's the hall.

existingCue.text: How will we choose between the hall and the marquee?

expected.reason: One of the two options no longer exists, so there is no choice left to ask about.

events.text: Could someone take the minutes today?
Yes, I'll take them.

expected.reason: The request is answered by the next line, so there is nothing to prompt.

events.text: Someone should water the seedlings over the weekend, and Priya has already said she'll do it.

expected.reason: The same line names who is doing it.

events.text: We still need someone to order the compost.
Leave the compost with me, I'll get it ordered today.

expected.reason: A speaker takes the task on, in words other than the question's.

events.text: Dana, could you send the invoice to the printer by Thursday?

expected.reason: The request is put to Dana by name, not to the user.

events.text: I think Dana should answer this one: who will run the stall on Sunday?

expected.reason: The speaker hands the question to Dana before asking it.

events.text: Dana has the keys sorted. Robin, what do you think about moving the stall indoors?

expected.reason: The question is put to the user by name.

events.text: What about you Robin, can you cover Saturday morning?

expected.reason: The question is put to the user by name, though no comma sets the name off.

events.text: Robin and Dana were both at the site visit. Can you tell us how it went?

expected.reason: "You" could mean either of the two people just named.

events.text: Robin's group already looked at the fence quotes, didn't they?

expected.reason: The user is spoken about, and it is unclear whether the question is for them.

events.text: Someone should chase the caterer.
As I said, we need somebody to chase the caterer.

expected.reason: The same need is restated; a second question would duplicate the one on screen.

events.text: Does anyone have the code for the gate?
Sorry, does anybody have the gate code?

expected.reason: An open question to the group is worth showing once; the repeat adds nothing.

events.text: We could do either a quiz night or a film night.
Anyway, that's enough about the social. Treasurer's report next.

existingCue.text: How will we choose between a quiz night and a film night?

expected.reason: The speaker closes the subject and starts the next agenda item.

events.text: Someone should phone the council about the skip.
Before we move on, can we agree who is phoning the council?

expected.reason: The speaker stays on the subject and asks the same thing; it is still unanswered.

events.text: Someone can always tell when the bread is fresh. It was lovely last week.

expected.reason: A remark about bread; no task is waiting for an owner.

events.text: The new shed arrived and it looks great.
Lovely. We'll see you all soon, thanks for coming.

expected.reason: A goodbye; "soon" is not a deadline anyone needs to pin down.

events.text: Thanks everyone, the minutes from last time are approved.
Great, and the accounts were signed off in March.

expected.reason: Finished business, with nothing open.

events.text: Nobody has picked up the banner printing yet, and the fair is on the 14th.

expected.reason: A task with a date coming and no owner, said without the word "someone".
